# 2 Baruch Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** First Fast and Vision

---

**1** I answered: "Lord, you have shown me how time unfolds and what is coming. You told me that the nations will face their reckoning.

**2** But I look around and see that those who sinned are many, and they lived comfortably, died peacefully, and left this world without consequence. Only a few nations are still standing.

**3** Meanwhile, many of the righteous have been taken joyfully into the age to come — but many more who are still alive are in agony.

**4** What is the point? We are alive and watching the suffering, waiting for a promised reward.

**5** How long will this go on? When will what was promised actually arrive?

**6** This world is nothing but exhaustion and trouble. Decay and death are the only constants.

**7** We arrive in pain and we leave in pain. Our whole life is one long struggle.

**8** But why? What for? Why be born at all if you are only going to leave in grief?

**9** Lord my God, let me ask you this: will there ever come a time when it will be said that the Most High actually regretted creating humanity — for the sake of all who have suffered?

**10** If you never intended your creation to come into existence, what was the point of speaking about a world to come?

**11** And if you didn't mean for everything to work out in the end, what was the purpose of calling a people your firstborn, a people you loved?

**12** What good is being called a chosen people if the sword is what they get?

**13** Why did you spread the Law of Moses throughout the world and promise an age that would never end?

**14** Because this world you made has not yet been brought to justice. You take no delight in what you have made.

**15** The light that was once lit for us has gone out. All we see is darkness and suffering.

**16** The world that was made for us is dark to us now. Zion's roads are in turmoil.

**17** The light of Zion has been extinguished. Zion's foundations have been shaken.

**18** Not one of the good things came to us. The full weight of disaster has fallen on us instead.

**19** So I will speak plainly before you, Lord my God. You know this yourself — before you ever created the world, you set up a judgment seat for everyone who would live in it."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. Vv.6-8 rendered as short declarative sentences for cumulative impact. V.9 "regretted creating" for "held back from creating" — the theodicy question made direct. The Syriac argument rendered for modern philosophical accessibility.*
